components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Blue pill action used for adding to cart, checkout, and continuing shopping.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #2563eb; color: #fff; border: 0; border-radius: 9999px; padding: 14px 16px; font: 500 0.875rem/1.25rem Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; transition: background-color 300ms ease-in-out; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #1d4ed8; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #a3a3a3; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Search Input
components.description: Compact bordered search field used in the desktop navigation.
components.css: .ds-input-search { width: 100%; background: #fff; color: #000; border: 1px solid #e5e5e5; border-radius: 8px; padding: 8px 16px; font: 400 0.875rem/1.25rem Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-input-search::placeholder { color: #737373; } .ds-input-search:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #a3a3a3; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Product Tile
components.description: Square product image frame with a floating title and price label.
components.css: .ds-product-tile { position: relative; display: block; aspect-ratio: 1; overflow: hidden; background: #fff; border: 1px solid #e5e5e5; border-radius: 8px; } .ds-product-tile:hover { border-color: #2563eb; } .ds-product-image { position: absolute; inset: 0; background: #fff; } .ds-product-label { position: absolute; left: 16px; right: 16px; bottom: 16px; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 8px; padding: 4px; border: 1px solid #e5e5e5; border-radius: 9999px; background: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.7); color: #000; font: 600 0.75rem/1rem Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; backdrop-filter: blur(12px); } .ds-product-label strong { flex: none; padding: 8px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #2563eb; color: #fff; font-weight: 600; }

narrative.overview:
Acme Store follows the restrained, reference-faithful language of Vercel Commerce: product imagery does the visual speaking while the interface stays crisp, neutral, and easy to scan. Inter typography, generous white space, thin neutral borders, and a single blue action color keep discovery and purchase steps legible without adding decorative layers.

The system is functional and lightly tactile. Images sit inside stable square frames, labels float over imagery, and controls become more distinct through border, color, and focus-state changes rather than heavy ornament. Light mode uses a near-white paper ground; dark mode inverts the same neutral structure with black surfaces and charcoal borders.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral-first storefront with one blue action accent.
Square, bordered product presentation with full-image visibility.
Rounded controls and compact sans-serif hierarchy.
Flat surfaces by default; elevation is reserved for the cart panel.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Blue carries action, selection, and price emphasis; neutral tones carry structure and supporting information.

rules.name: The Compact Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Keep storefront text small and scannable; use weight and contrast to distinguish actions from metadata rather than oversized headings.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Use borders and tonal surfaces for ordinary hierarchy; reserve a shadow for a surface that must float above the page.

dos: Do keep product imagery inside square, bordered frames and use `object-contain` when the complete image must remain visible.
Do use Commerce Blue for actions, selection, hover emphasis, and price pills rather than introducing extra accent colors.
Do preserve the 4px spacing rhythm and the 8px/12px/16px radius progression evidenced by the components.
Do retain visible focus treatment on links, inputs, and buttons.
Do keep light and dark surfaces structurally parallel: near-white/white in light mode and near-black/black in dark mode.
donts: Don't crop or distort catalog imagery to fill a tile.
Don't add decorative shadows to ordinary cards or page sections; depth is intentionally restrained.
Don't replace compact Inter hierarchy with display typography or oversized marketing headlines.
Don't introduce a second dominant accent without a product-level reason; the existing system is neutral-first and blue-led.
Don't turn a product label into layout content; it floats over the image and must not shift the tile geometry.
